code: if (!requireNamespace("sf")) install.packages("sf") if (!requireNamespace("leaflet")) install.packages("leaflet") library(parzer) lats <- c(   "46.4183",   "46.4383° N",   "46.5683° N",   "46° 27´ 5.4\" N",   "46° 25.56’",   "N46°24’4.333" ) lons <- c(   "25.7391",   "E25°34’6.4533",   "25.3391° E",   "25.8391° E",   "25° 35.56’",   "E25°34’4.333" ) dat <- data.frame(   longitude = parse_lon(lons),   latitude = parse_lat(lats) ) dat ##   longitude latitude ## 1  25.73910  46.4183 ## 2  25.56846  46.4383 ## 3  25.33910  46.5683 ## 4  25.83910  46.4515 ## 5  25.59267  46.4260 ## 6  25.56787  46.4012 dat$shape <- c("round", "square", "triangle", "round", "square", "square") dat$color <- c("blue", "yellow", "green", "red", "green", "yellow") dat ##   longitude latitude    shape  color ## 1  25.73910  46.4183    round   blue ## 2  25.56846  46.4383   square yellow ## 3  25.33910  46.5683 triangle  green ## 4  25.83910  46.4515    round    red ## 5  25.59267  46.4260   square  green ## 6  25.56787  46.4012   square yellow datsf <- sf::st_as_sf(dat, coords = c("longitude", "latitude")) datsf ## Simple feature collection with 6 features and 2 fields ## Geometry type: POINT ## Dimension:     XY ## Bounding box:  xmin: 25.3391 ymin: 46.4012 xmax: 25.8391 ymax: 46.5683 ## CRS:           NA ##      shape  color                 geometry ## 1    round   blue  POINT (25.7391 46.4183) ## 2   square yellow POINT (25.56846 46.4383) ## 3 triangle  green  POINT (25.3391 46.5683) ## 4    round    red  POINT (25.8391 46.4515) ## 5   square  green  POINT (25.59267 46.426) ## 6   square yellow POINT (25.56787 46.4012) center_lon <- mean(dat$longitude) center_lat <- mean(dat$latitude) library("leaflet") leaflet() |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(data = datsf) |>   setView(center_lon, center_lat, zoom = 10) bbox <- c(   xmin = 25.42813, ymin = 46.39455,   xmax = 25.68769, ymax = 46.60346 ) leaflet() |>   addTiles() |>   addRectangles(bbox[["xmin"]], bbox[["ymin"]], bbox[["xmax"]], bbox[["ymax"]]) |>   setView(center_lon, center_lat, zoom = 10) datsf_c <- sf::st_crop(datsf, bbox) Warning: attribute variables are assumed to be spatially constant throughout all geometries leaflet() |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(data = datsf_c) |>   setView(center_lon, center_lat, zoom = 10)

text: pattern describes values written. made letters characters. idea comes AngleFormat Apache SIS CLongLatString. D, M S stand digits whole degrees, minutes seconds. number letters exact number digits: DD means exactly 2 digits, reads "05" "5", DDD means exactly 3 digits, longitudes often need. Values written without leading zeros need second pattern, example c("DD MM SSH", "D MM SSH") reads "45 03 02N" "5 03 02N". D required. M S optional, S needs M, come order D, M, S. d, m s stand decimal digits degrees, minutes seconds. last unit can . come right , "DDMMmmm", dot follows , "DDMM.m". Without dot, decimal point written value. number letters exact number decimal digits: way know hidden decimal point . "HDDMMmmmmm" reads "N455698735" N 45 degrees 56.98735 minutes. dot, value decimal point one decimal digits, many like: "DDMM.m" reads "4556.9" "4556.98735". H stands hemisphere letter: N S parse_lat(), E W parse_lon(), upper lower case. S W give negative value. H can start, end middle, . letter pair, example E parse_lat(), gives NA. space matches one spaces (white space). character, example °, ', ", :, dot followed d, m s, must value exactly pattern. sign can always written right degrees: +, -, Unicode minus (U+2212), en dash – em dash —. H, rules format = NULL: "-45S" "+45S" give -45, "-45N" gives NA, minus sign letter disagree. Spaces start end value ignored. pattern matched value given: cleaning done format = NULL, example reading d º degree mark, happen. value gives NA match pattern, minutes seconds 60 , result range (latitude outside -90/90, longitude outside -180/360). values listed one warning. read format = NULL. missing value (NA) empty string gives NA without warning. pattern work, example "MMDD", "DDmmSS" "DDX", error. Numbers turned text first, lose leading zeros: parse_lon(0002741, format = "DDDMMSS") sees "2741" gives NA. Give values text: parse_lon("0002741", format = "DDDMMSS"). See Format examples section many examples.

title: Parse latitude values — parse_lat
code: parse_lat("") #> [1] NA  # with format: say how the values are written (see the Format section) parse_lat("512839N", format = "DDMMSSH") # ICAO => 51.4775 #> [1] 51.4775 parse_lat("4556.98735", format = "DDMM.mmmmm") # NMEA => 45.94979 #> [1] 45.94979 # after a dot, any number of decimals parse_lat(c("4556.9", "4556.98735"), format = "DDMM.m") #> [1] 45.94833 45.94979 # no dot: 5 letters, so exactly 5 decimals => 45.94979 parse_lat("N455698735", format = "HDDMMmmmmm") #> [1] 45.94979 parse_lat("2343 56N", format = "DDMM SSH") # => 23.73222 #> [1] 23.73222 parse_lat("23 4356N", format = "DD MMSSH") # => 23.73222 #> [1] 23.73222 parse_lat("2343.5N", format = "DDMM.mH") # => 23.725 #> [1] 23.725 parse_lat("45N54.2356", format = "DDHMM.m") # => 45.90393 #> [1] 45.90393 parse_lat("40°25'06\"N", format = "DD°MM'SS\"H") # => 40.41833 #> [1] 40.41833 parse_lat(c("-45S", "+45S"), format = "DDH") # => -45 -45 #> [1] -45 -45 parse_lat(4530, format = "DDMM") # numbers work too => 45.5 #> [1] 45.5 # several formats, tried in order for each value parse_lat(c("4530", "45 30", "N4530"), format = c("DDMM", "DD MM", "HDDMM")) #> [1] 45.5 45.5 45.5 # no leading zero: a second format with one D parse_lat(c("45 03 02N", "5 03 02N"), format = c("DD MM SSH", "D MM SSH")) #> [1] 45.050556  5.050556 # NA and one warning: sign and letter disagree, wrong letter, 75 minutes parse_lat(c("-45N", "45E", "4575"), format = c("DDH", "DDMM")) #> Warning: NA for 3 value(s) that could not be read with `format`: #>   "-45N": minus sign and direction letter disagree #>   "45E": direction letter must be N or S #>   "4575": minutes or seconds not within 0/60 range #> [1] NA NA NA # without format, packed digits give NA and a warning that points to format parse_lat("2343 56N") #> Warning: not within -90/90 range, got: 2343 56n #>   degrees, minutes and seconds may be packed together (e.g. DDMMSS): try the format argument of parse_lat() or parse_lon() #> [1] NA  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ parse_lat("-91") parse_lat("95") parse_lat("asdfaf")  parse_lat("45") parse_lat("-45") parse_lat("-45.2323")  # out of range with std::stod? parse_lat("-45.23232e24") parse_lat("-45.23232e2")  # numeric input parse_lat(1:10) parse_lat(85:94)  # different formats parse_lat("40.4183318 N") parse_lat("40.4183318 S") parse_lat("40 25 5.994") # => 40.41833  parse_lat("40.4183318N") parse_lat("N40.4183318") parse_lat("40.4183318S") parse_lat("S40.4183318")  parse_lat("N 39 21.440") # => 39.35733 parse_lat("S 56 1.389") # => -56.02315  parse_lat("N40°25’5.994") # => 40.41833 parse_lat("40° 25´ 5.994\" N") # => 40.41833 parse_lat("40:25:6N") parse_lat("40:25:5.994N") parse_lat("40d 25’ 6\" N") } # }

title: parse string with lat and lon together — parse_llstr
text: order = "auto" (default), direction letters N, S, E W (upper lower case) say coordinate comes first: latitude first, letter ("45.5, -74.5"), letters fit ("N45.5, W74.5", "45.5, 74.5W") longitude first, letters fit : first part E W, second part N S ("W74.5, N45.5", "74.5W, 45.5", "-74.5, 45.5N"). one part letter, part decides. NA values, warning, letters contradict : "E45, E30", "N45, N30" order = "lat_lon" order = "lon_lat", order forced. Use strings longitude first letters: parse_llstr("-74.5, 45.5", order = "lon_lat"). string letters fit forced order gives NA values, warning: "N45.5, W74.5" order = "lon_lat".

H right two coordinates goes first one, "DDMMSSHDDDMMSSH", unless first one already H. goes second one, "HD.ddddHDDD.ddd", reads "N4.9196E101.347". coordinates follow order. "lon_lat", first one longitude, "DDDMMSSH DDMMSSH". "auto", H letters say one latitude, pattern without H means latitude first. number D letters decide. string matched : cleaned, cut comma space, format = NULL. Spaces start end ignored. Strings match pattern, give NA one value , listed one warning. read format = NULL. pattern work error, example "DDMMSS" (one D block) "DDMMSSHH DDDMMSSH" (two H one coordinate).

DMS parse_llstr("N4 51'36\", E101 34'7\"") #>    lat      lon #> 1 4.86 101.5686 parse_llstr(c("4 51'36\"S, 101 34'7\"W", "N4 51'36\", E101 34'7\"")) #>     lat       lon #> 1 -4.86 -101.5686 #> 2  4.86  101.5686 parse_llstr("4:51:36S 101:34:7W") #>     lat       lon #> 1 -4.86 -101.5686  # which coordinate comes first (see the Order section) parse_llstr("W101.347, N4.9196") # the letters say longitude first #>      lat      lon #> 1 4.9196 -101.347 parse_llstr("101.347E, 4.9196") # one letter is enough #>      lat     lon #> 1 4.9196 101.347 parse_llstr("-101.347, 4.9196", order = "lon_lat") # no letters: say it #>      lat      lon #> 1 4.9196 -101.347 # NA and a warning: the letters contradict each other parse_llstr("E45, E30") #> Warning: direction letters contradict each other, got: E45, E30 #>   lat lon #> 1  NA  NA # NA for both, and a warning: 101.347 is not a latitude, so the values # are probably swapped parse_llstr("101.347, 4.9196") #> Warning: not within -90/90 range, got: 101.347 #>   check that you did not invert lon and lat #> Warning: latitude out of range but valid as a longitude, so longitude may come first: try order = "lon_lat", got: 101.347, 4.9196 #>   lat lon #> 1  NA  NA parse_llstr("101.347, 4.9196", order = "lon_lat") #>      lat     lon #> 1 4.9196 101.347 # one part cannot be read: the other one is kept parse_llstr("abc, -74.5") #> Warning: no digits detected, got: abc #>   lat   lon #> 1  NA -74.5  # with format: one pattern for the whole string (see the Format section) parse_llstr("512839N 0002741W", format = "DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH") # ICAO #>       lat        lon #> 1 51.4775 -0.4613889 parse_llstr("512839N0002741W", format = "DDMMSSHDDDMMSSH") # no separator #>       lat        lon #> 1 51.4775 -0.4613889 parse_llstr("4916.45,N,12311.12,W", format = "DDMM.m,H,DDDMM.m,H") # NMEA #>        lat       lon #> 1 49.27417 -123.1853 parse_llstr("N4.9196E101.347", format = "HD.ddddHDDD.ddd") #>      lat     lon #> 1 4.9196 101.347 # longitude first: the letters decide parse_llstr("0002741W 512839N", format = "DDDMMSSH DDMMSSH") #>       lat        lon #> 1 51.4775 -0.4613889 # longitude first, without letters parse_llstr("101.347 4.9196", format = "DDD.d D.d", order = "lon_lat") #>      lat     lon #> 1 4.9196 101.347 # several formats, tried in order for each string parse_llstr(   c("512839N 0002741W", "512839N0002741W", "51 28 39N 000 27 41W"),   format = c("DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH", "DDMMSSHDDDMMSSH", "DD MM SSH DDD MM SSH") ) #>       lat        lon #> 1 51.4775 -0.4613889 #> 2 51.4775 -0.4613889 #> 3 51.4775 -0.4613889 # NA and one warning: 75 minutes (the longitude is kept), and two # latitude letters parse_llstr(   c("517539N 0002741W", "512839N 0002741N"),   format = "DDMMSSH DDDMMSSH" ) #> Warning: NA for 2 value(s) that could not be read with `format`: #>   "517539N 0002741W": latitude: minutes or seconds not within 0/60 range #>   "512839N 0002741N": direction letters contradict each other #>   lat        lon #> 1  NA -0.4613889 #> 2  NA         NA # without format, a string with no separator gives NA and a warning parse_llstr("N4.9196E101.347") #> Warning: could not split into latitude and longitude, got: N4.9196E101.347 #>   lat lon #> 1  NA  NA  # add both columns with one call, picking them by name df <- data.frame(x = c("N4.9196, E101.347", "4.9196 -101.347")) cbind(df, parse_llstr(str = df[["x"]])[c("lat", "lon")]) #>                   x    lat      lon #> 1 N4.9196, E101.347 4.9196  101.347 #> 2   4.9196 -101.347 4.9196 -101.347 # dplyr:      df |> dplyr::mutate(parse_llstr(str = x)[c("lat", "lon")]) # data.table: dt[, c("lat", "lon") := parse_llstr(str = x)[c("lat", "lon")]]

title: Parse longitude values — parse_lon
text: pattern describes values written. made letters characters. idea comes AngleFormat Apache SIS CLongLatString. D, M S stand digits whole degrees, minutes seconds. number letters exact number digits: DD means exactly 2 digits, reads "05" "5", DDD means exactly 3 digits, longitudes often need. Values written without leading zeros need second pattern, example c("DD MM SSH", "D MM SSH") reads "45 03 02N" "5 03 02N". D required. M S optional, S needs M, come order D, M, S. d, m s stand decimal digits degrees, minutes seconds. last unit can . come right , "DDMMmmm", dot follows , "DDMM.m". Without dot, decimal point written value. number letters exact number decimal digits: way know hidden decimal point . "HDDMMmmmmm" reads "N455698735" N 45 degrees 56.98735 minutes. dot, value decimal point one decimal digits, many like: "DDMM.m" reads "4556.9" "4556.98735". H stands hemisphere letter: N S parse_lat(), E W parse_lon(), upper lower case. S W give negative value. H can start, end middle, . letter pair, example E parse_lat(), gives NA. space matches one spaces (white space). character, example °, ', ", :, dot followed d, m s, must value exactly pattern. sign can always written right degrees: +, -, Unicode minus (U+2212), en dash – em dash —. H, rules format = NULL: "-45S" "+45S" give -45, "-45N" gives NA, minus sign letter disagree. Spaces start end value ignored. pattern matched value given: cleaning done format = NULL, example reading d º degree mark, happen. value gives NA match pattern, minutes seconds 60 , result range (latitude outside -90/90, longitude outside -180/360). values listed one warning. read format = NULL. missing value (NA) empty string gives NA without warning. pattern work, example "MMDD", "DDmmSS" "DDX", error. Numbers turned text first, lose leading zeros: parse_lon(0002741, format = "DDDMMSS") sees "2741" gives NA. Give values text: parse_lon("0002741", format = "DDDMMSS"). See Format examples section many examples.

what: parzer: Parse Messy Geographic Coordinates — parzer-package
title: parzer: Parse Messy Geographic Coordinates — parzer-package
text: Parse messy geographic coordinates various character formats decimal degree numeric values. Parse coordinates parts (degree, minutes, seconds); calculate hemisphere coordinates; pull individually degrees, minutes, seconds; add subtract degrees, minutes, seconds. C++ code herein originally inspired code written Jeffrey D. Bogan, completely re-written. 'format' argument reads packed digits, coordinates International Civil Aviation Organization ('ICAO') GPS receivers ('NMEA').

title: parzer 0.5.0
text: parse_lat() parse_lon() (functions built ) now return NA warning minutes seconds within 0/60, instead silently converting , e.g. “10°30,12345” (#60). Negative minutes seconds, decimal degree minute followed another slot (e.g. “45.5 30”), now also give NA warning. comma separator, decimal mark; now documented. parse_parts_lat() parse_parts_lon() (pz_degree(), pz_minute(), pz_second()) longer lose sign values -1 0: sign now sits first non-zero part, e.g. -0.5 gives deg 0, min -30. also longer return 60 seconds, e.g. 10.35 now 10 deg 21 min 0 sec, 10 deg 20 min 60 sec. parse_llstr() now gives one clear warning (“split latitude longitude”) string split, keeps rows. , string gave two confusing “digits” warnings internal marker. warning text invalid letter degrees uses plain ASCII quotes. parse_lon_lat() parse_hemisphere() now clean symbols like ° way parse_lat() parse_lon() (, “40°25’” gave 40).
